> This feels like a workaround for a Frontend issue. If it is marked `optional`, then the frontend should be able to return `None`.
> 
> I therefore do not support the change as it is proposed, but I am not familiar enough with Frontend code to propose a better solution.

I do agree, originally I had all of these return a 'None' value, which then had to be intercepted as a key removal. It felt weird though, especially as it meant you always had to choose 'None', and every other UI I've used within HA just allows an empty entry, I didn't want to make it inconsistent. It does feel like the wrong approach but I can't see a clean 'allow None' in config flow without having the options set to custom_value (custom value is what seems to enable the cross to negate the selected value). Additionally, it then felt weird because I'd need two methods to handle it, as the measurement input is legitimately a custom value and should allow empty (which it currently doesn't, as it retains the old value due to the options key not being cleared).

Happy to change however, and really hoped there was just a nice 'allow None' option that enabled the cross but still enforced the list options.
Have a look around other selector implementations - see if there is something you can duplicate.

If it's optional it's not part of the user_input hence the update doesn't consider those keys.
I think this should be solved with a few if's in the `validate_sensor_edit` to pop keys if they are not part of `user_input`

> If it's optional it's not part of the user_input hence the update doesn't consider those keys. I think this should be solved with a few if's in the `validate_sensor_edit` to pop keys if they are not part of `user_input`

I may not have the best understanding for this PR. Effectively it seemed the problem was that things like 'device_class' only gave the fixed options from the enum. This was fine on creation as by default it's empty, but as soon as populated there is no 'empty' option. The only ways I could see to handle this with the config_flow were:

1) add an extra enum value. The value itself cannot be None apparently, so it would have to have an actual value and then be handled within validate.
2) the way I did in this, which is to allow a 'custom value' so as to get the UI to allow text entry and clearing rather than only the fixed set of drop-down values. This of course left a problem if you then put in a value not present in the enum.

Both of these honestly feel untidy, and ideally what I was looking for was 'use these values, or clear it if not entered', effectively being able to choose a value from the enum of hit the 'x' to clear it. Which is basically the behaviour of creating a new sensor as the UI doesn't enforce an enum value until the first time you pick it. I haven't had chance yet to see how others are approaching this, I did of course look around when implementing as it felt unclean both ways but I'll take another look and see if there's a better option.
Maybe easiest is to add empty string to dropdown, and then replace empty strings with None on validation.

> Maybe easiest is to add empty string to dropdown, and then replace empty strings with None on validation.

Yeah I'll change to this and see how it behaves.

As it's optional one can clear the field hence the user_input is missing the key (it's optional). 
Maybe not the best for the user so adding and empty string to the list is perhaps easier for a user to choose instead of erasing.

> As it's optional one can clear the field hence the user_input is missing the key (it's optional). Maybe not the best for the user so adding and empty string to the list is perhaps easier for a user to choose instead of erasing.

Oh no, am I being incredibly stupid? In the live deployed version it uses optional, and I couldn't even see a way of removing the value once it were set, there's no 'X' or empty option, hence the silly hoops I've jumped through. Am I overlooking something really obvious?

> Oh no, am I being incredibly stupid? In the live deployed version it uses optional, and I couldn't even see a way of removing the value once it were set, there's no 'X' or empty option, hence the silly hoops I've jumped through. Am I overlooking something really obvious?

One can just remove the content from the field manually.
However the current code doesn't deal with missing key's from `user_input` so therefore nothing changes and the key is still saved.
But I would also think perhaps an empty string to select is more user friendly than the user erasing the content from the field.

> > Oh no, am I being incredibly stupid? In the live deployed version it uses optional, and I couldn't even see a way of removing the value once it were set, there's no 'X' or empty option, hence the silly hoops I've jumped through. Am I overlooking something really obvious?
>

But I would also think perhaps an empty string to select is more user friendly than the user erasing the content from the field.

I'll do just that when I get back yeah. I just can't see any way to manually remove the content, not without doing something silly like using developer tools anyway, so I wasn't sure how the UI intended this

@epenet @gjohansson-ST Thanks for both of your input. I've been playing around with the empty value option and remembered why it didn't work for me now, as that was my original approach.

1) Config flow doesn't allow a None value, it must be a str
2) If the value is "", it actually disregards it entirely and retains the previous value. For example, if the value is currently "date", and I try and set it to "", the value in the dict will still be "date".

The only option I can think to have this particular type of UI is to define a const str we can identify later as 'remove the key entirely', which I believe can have a label of "", and then in the case of the value being equal to that, it'll then pop the item out of the options dict. That feels like a smell also if I'm honest, but I'm happy to go with the option you prefer.

This is only really because I still can't see how you're supposed to clear the enum value on an optional dropdown. If you can confirm this is actually possible and I'm just missing something I'd greatly appreciate it, as I cannot see a way to clear it in the UI as it currently stands and if that exists, that half solves the issue. This may be an issue with HA frontend, as I'd expect the vol.Optional on a SelectSelector to allow me to clear it, even if we need to handle it in the validate to actually remove the option key.

There are no other components that use an optional 'SelectSelector' (all other cases appear to use it as a required), other than MQTT, which I don't believe has the same issue as you cannot edit the value in question later. As such, I have no good example component to base on.

I could be missing something but to summarise it appears the following are the only ways to progress this one:

1) Raise the bug on HA frontend and hope a nice way to clear is implemented (which should be the correct way), unless I'm missing this. In the mean time users must delete the sensor to clear device type/class (I can still fix unit of measurement as that's a custom_value).
2) Use the current PR method, where it's a validated 'custom_value', which grants the UI 'x' button to clear it but only allows valid enum values to be submitted from the dropdown, or typed/copy-pasted.
3) Add an empty str labelled dict item with a constant unique str value to identify it as 'to be removed' from the options dict later.

review_comments: The key is the adjusted suggestion above: simply handling when the key is missing from the user-input, and removing the corresponding item manually.

It looks like simply adding an empty option solves the situation.
I think it should be resolved in frontend - but maybe this works for now.

```suggestion
            options=[
                SelectOptionDict(value=item.value, label=item.value)
                for item in SensorDeviceClass
            ]
            + [SelectOptionDict(value="", label="")],
```

> It looks like simply adding an empty option solves the situation. I think it should be resolved in frontend - but maybe this works for now.

Thanks, but just to check did you test this? I know there have been some UI changes of late, so perhaps it now works, but in my testing, an empty entry is entirely disregarded (see my comment https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/84482#issuecomment-1366258367 ). This was of course my original idea as it seemed the most logical. The only option I could find is to pass _some_ value in, and then use that value to instead be interpreted as a deletion of the original key, otherwise it just retains the old value.
I used "None" in another integration for a user to choose and then had a validation to remove the key if that choice was made.

Sorry - you are correct. The frontend was kind of working correctly but not storing in the storage.
I do have it working now with the simple:
```python
    vol.Optional(CONF_DEVICE_CLASS): SelectSelector(
        SelectSelectorConfig(
            options=[""] + [cls.value for cls in SensorDeviceClass],
            mode=SelectSelectorMode.DROPDOWN,
        )
    ),
    vol.Optional(CONF_STATE_CLASS): SelectSelector(
        SelectSelectorConfig(
            options=[""] + [cls.value for cls in SensorStateClass],
            mode=SelectSelectorMode.DROPDOWN,
        )
    ),
    vol.Optional(CONF_UNIT_OF_MEASUREMENT): SelectSelector(
        SelectSelectorConfig(
            options=[cls.value for cls in UnitOfTemperature],
            custom_value=True,
            mode=SelectSelectorMode.DROPDOWN,
        )
    ),
```
